title: [CQ-R13f1] Certify check-containment runs
description:
Objective: add the 'check-containment' certify check. It shows, on real hardware, that the check identity stays contained. This covers CQ-R13f DoD item 2.

Split out of CQ-R13f (task-d45d52c0) by architect-899a90d6 on 2026-10-30, approved by the human in the architect REPL: R13f's three checks measured about 470 changed lines. R13f keeps 'writer-containment' and 'controller-replacement', depends on this task, and re-verifies all three at its own QA.

Deliverable:
- scripts/local-runner/certify-containment.mjs (new) exports CONTAINMENT_CHECKS = [check-containment], spliced into certify.mjs BODY after BRIDGE_CHECKS. R13f later adds its two checks around it in the same module.
- The certify context gains platform (the observed platform), cacheDir and supervisor (the real bytes): the names R13h and R13g already expect.

'check-containment' runs runCheckJob three times on one generated snapshot (a probe script, one protected file, one tracked unprotected file). Each run gets its own fresh VM, and the check stops at the first failing run.
1. Probe run. The approved command runs the probe script, which exits 0 only when every refusal holds: no network interface but lo and no route out of the private netns; reading the supervisor credential is refused with a permission error; writing the protected file fails with EROFS; RLIMIT_NPROC and RLIMIT_FSIZE equal CHECK_BOUNDARIES and cannot be raised, and a write at the FSIZE limit fails with EFBIG. The run must resolve 'passed' with workspace 'intact'.
2. Integrity run (human decision, 2026-10-30). The command tries to overwrite the protected file, which the read-only mount refuses, then waits for the file to change. Once the session has started (its first stdout bytes), the certify host changes the protected file as root in the guest's own mount namespace. The supervisor's after-run hash check must catch it, so the run must resolve 'inconclusive'. On a correct guest the job alone can never change a protected file, so this is the only native way to exercise the after-run check and the exit-80 path.
3. Edit run. The command edits the tracked unprotected file. The run must resolve 'passed' with workspace 'changed'.
Every run must end with vm 'deleted' and failure null. Each outcome maps to a fixed code; a runCheckJob rejection keeps its own stable code.

Tests in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs use fake runCheckJob results through a test-only deps.containment seam. The native behavior is certified only by the operator run.

Out of scope:
- writer-containment and controller-replacement (CQ-R13f);
- cancellation and recovery (CQ-R13h); the canary toolchain check (CQ-R13g);
- enabling verified-local;
- .moe edits.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs
definitionOfDone: 'check-containment' passes only when the probe run resolves 'passed' with workspace 'intact', the integrity run resolves 'inconclusive', and the edit run resolves 'passed' with workspace 'changed', each with vm 'deleted' and failure null. Any other outcome fails with a fixed code and starts no later run. Shown by tests with fake runCheckJob results.

Each run gets the generated snapshot, its exact check frame (one protected entry carrying the file's git blob oid), dependencies [], a fresh synthetic owner and credential, and the certify context's platform, base ledger, cacheDir, supervisor and provider. The integrity run changes the protected file only after its session's first stdout bytes, through one fixed root argv. Shown by tests.

The certify context carries platform, cacheDir and supervisor. CERTIFY_CHECKS lists 'check-containment' after 'guest-network' with teardown last, and the updated CF rows, including the all-pass CF1, pass.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

SHARED-FILE RULES
- Before editing, cp scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs to a scratch dir, and measure your own delta against that copy (peers may add hunks).
- Edit local-runner.test.mjs ONLY with the Edit tool (the contested-path TOOL witness, mem gotcha-local-runner-size-rails). Never write it from Bash, sed or python.

HARNESS. Declare everything next to CERTIFY_IDS, BEFORE certifyHarness. A filtered run (--test-name-pattern '^CF' or '^CC') starts its first test during module evaluation, so nothing certifyHarness reads synchronously may be a const declared later in the file (TDZ).
- CERTIFY_IDS gains 'check-containment' before 'teardown'. BRIDGE_NOT_RUN gains ['check-containment', 'not-run'].
- CHANGE_ARGV = ['sudo', '-n', 'truncate', '-s', '0', '/var/lib/moe/workspace/moe-certify/protected.txt'], spelled out literally.
- isChange = args => args[0] === 'exec' && args[4] === 'sudo' && args[6] === 'truncate'.
- function containmentRig(runs = []) returns { calls, containment: { runCheckJob } }. Its fake runCheckJob(input, given):
  - records { input, given } (call index at: 0 probe, 1 integrity, 2 edit);
  - reads { session = at === 1, reject, ...result } = { workspace: ['intact', 'unverified', 'changed'][at], ...runs[at] };
  - when reject is set, throws Object.assign(new Error('/private/path'), { code: reject });
  - when session is set, observed = await given.session({ name: nameAt(7 + at), check: input.check, provider: input.provider, budgetMs: input.budgetMs, timeoutMs: 1_000 }). That is the REAL runCheckSession, through the check's wrapper, over the harness router, exactly as runCheckJob calls its session step;
  - resolves Object.freeze({ outcome: 'passed', exitCode: 0, signal: null, outputTail: '', ...observed, environment: null, instance: nameAt(7 + at), vm: 'deleted', failure: null, executionReady: false, ...result }).
- certifyHarness gains two options: `containment` (the rig's runs) and `change` (the answer for the change argv; default answering('')).
  - Its run records an isChange call with changes.push([[...args], options]) and answers it BEFORE delegating to fake.run, because fakeGuest throws on a foreign instance.
  - Never record it in `probes`: GN1 and GN3 pin probes exactly.
  - deps gains containment: rig.containment; the return value gains changes and rig.
- BRIDGE_SCRIPTS gains 'certify-integrity': proc => { proc.send(CB_HELLO); setImmediate(() => { proc.send(cbExit(0)); proc.exit(80); }); }. That is hello, the job's exit-0 observation, then the supervisor's PROTECTED_CHANGED 80, which runCheckSession classifies as 'inconclusive'.
- Every pinned id list or not-run tail gains the new id:
  - CF3 `undeleted` gets ['check-containment', 'passed'] before the failed teardown;
  - CB1's literal CERTIFY_CHECKS list;
  - CB6 failedBridge and networkFailed get ['check-containment', 'not-run'];
  - GN5's checks list, and its `.slice(-5)` deep-equals ['bridge-framing', 'bridge-eof', 'guest-network', 'check-containment', 'teardown'].

BUNDLE. scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs: `shipped` gains 'certify-containment.mjs'. It does NOT go in `required`, which the onboarding refusal row walks. Name CQ-R13f1 in the comment above it.

Error handling in the harness:
- the rig rejects only with a fixed code;
- the change answer is injectable for the failure rows;
- nothing reaches a real provider, the network or a VM.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
certify gains 'check-containment' after 'guest-network' (teardown stays last). It runs runCheckJob three times on one generated snapshot: moe-certify/probe.py, the protected moe-certify/protected.txt and the tracked moe-certify/tracked.txt. Each run is in its own fresh VM, with a fresh synthetic owner and credential, dependencies [], budgetMs c.bounds.sessionMs, and the context's platform (observed), base ledger, cacheDir, supervisor bytes and provider.

- Probe run: `python3 -I -B moe-certify/probe.py` must resolve passed/intact. It exits 10-14 for the first refusal that does not hold.
- Integrity run: at the session's first stdout bytes, the host runs a root `truncate -s 0` of the protected file in the guest's own mount namespace, once. The run must resolve inconclusive with exitCode 0 and the change witnessed.
- Edit run: must resolve passed/changed.

Every run needs vm 'deleted' and failure null. The first failing run stops the check with one fixed code; runCheckJob's own failure or rejection code is kept. The certify context gains platform, cacheDir and supervisor. Native evidence is operator-only; executionReady stays false.
acceptanceCriteria: check-containment passes only when probe=passed/intact, integrity=inconclusive with exitCode 0 and a successful change, and edit=passed/changed, each with vm 'deleted' and failure null (CC3, CC5).

Failures use fixed codes: CERTIFY_CONTAINMENT_VM_NOT_DELETED; runCheckJob's own non-null failure code; CERTIFY_CONTAINMENT_NETWORK/CREDENTIAL/PROTECTED/RLIMIT/FSIZE for probe exits 10-14; CERTIFY_CONTAINMENT_PROBE_FAILED, _CHANGE_FAILED, _INTEGRITY_FAILED and _EDIT_FAILED. A rejection keeps its stable code, and no later run starts (CC4, CC5).

Each run's input keys are exactly platform, ledger, owner, cacheDir, supervisor, credential, snapshot, check, budgetMs, onReady, dependencies and provider. check = {id, command, protected:[{path:'moe-certify/protected.txt', oid:'c847a247be38418490fff92ebf0fa678d21f99da'}]} (CC3).

The change argv is exactly ['exec','--no-map-working-directory',<run instance>,'--','sudo','-n','truncate','-s','0','/var/lib/moe/workspace/moe-certify/protected.txt'] with QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS. It is invoked once, and only after the integrity session's first stdout bytes (CC4).

The probe exits 0 only when every refusal holds, else 10-14 (CC2, stubbed). CERTIFY_CHECKS ends ['guest-network','check-containment','teardown'], and the updated CF1-CF3, CB1, CB6 and GN5 rows pass. The verification command exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.

teardown stays last and deletes only certify's main VM by its owned name. The runs get the base ledger, never the capturing wrapper.

No guest byte, host path or credential reaches a code, a message or the report. The native runCheckJob and runCheckSession behave unchanged: the only wrapper is the integrity session's spawn tee, which passes its argument and result through.

sourceAssumptions: check-lifecycle.mjs runCheckJob(input, {session,...}): it calls session({name, check, provider, budgetMs, timeoutMs, signal}) and resolves {outcome, exitCode, signal, outputTail, environment, workspace, instance, vm, failure, executionReady}. A pass without a verified delete becomes 'inconclusive'. check-session.mjs maps exit 80 after hello and one observation to 'inconclusive'.

guest-supervisor.py: run_bridge writes hello before GUARD starts the job. check_job runs holds(), reown and protect_mounts (RO file binds) before relay, and returns 80 when relay returned 0 and unchanged() is false. WORKSPACE = '/var/lib/moe/workspace'.

check-evidence.mjs CHECK_BOUNDARIES: interfaces ['lo'], RLIMIT_NPROC 2048, RLIMIT_FSIZE 1073741824, credential '/etc/moe/supervisor.credential'. lifecycle.mjs invoker uses provider.run and refuses a non-owned name; QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS is 30000. certify.mjs runCheck turns a throw into failed with stable(code).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Trigger the change on the job's first decoded stdout frame, or on the session's first raw stdout bytes (hello)? Chose hello, R13h's cancellation idiom. run_bridge writes hello after the before-run hash check and protect_mounts, so the change lands during the session and the after-run check must catch it. (2) Change with a shell append, or with a fixed `sudo -n truncate -s 0 <abs path>`? Chose truncate: no shell, and it keeps the inode, so the job's RO bind and the supervisor's view both see the change. (3) Pass the integrity run on outcome alone, or also require exitCode 0 and a change witness? Both added. check_job returns 80 for ANY changed protected path, so outcome alone would pass a job that overwrote the file itself, or a result that never ran a session. Single-rule rows pin both guards. (4) One code per run, or one per probe refusal? Probe exits 10-14 map to their own codes (4 lines), so the operator sees which boundary failed. (5) Remap runCheckJob infra failures, or keep them? Keep them, as bridge-framing and guest-network propagate TRANSFER_ and PROVIDER_ codes. (6) Test the probe through an unshare simulation, or through stubbed primitives? Stubbed: CI runners restrict unprivileged user namespaces. The architect ran the simulation once by hand. (7) Record the change in `probes`, or in a separate `changes` list? Separate, because GN1 and GN3 pin probes exactly. (8) One big tests step, or two? Two, because a step description is capped at 10000 chars.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- guest-supervisor.py check_job returns PROTECTED_CHANGED 80 whenever relay returned 0 and unchanged() is false, whatever the job's own exit. runCheckSession maps 80 after hello and one observation to 'inconclusive', with the observation's exitCode.
- runCheckJob turns a pass without a verified delete into 'inconclusive' with failure CHECK_VM_DELETE_FAILED. That is why the verdict checks the leak first.
- Linux open with O_TRUNC takes mnt_want_write before the permission check. 'wb' on a RO bind is EROFS; 'ab' and 'r+b' are EACCES (verified under unshare).
- Windows CI runs local-runner.test.mjs, so POSIX-only rows need an inline skip. NOT_POSIX is declared later in the file (TDZ).
- A filtered run starts its first test during module evaluation, so certifyHarness may read only consts declared before it.
- Pinned id lists: CERTIFY_IDS, BRIDGE_NOT_RUN, CF3 undeleted, CB1, CB6 failedBridge, networkFailed, GN5.
- The full prototype is Serena memory task-task-4e2ab1584c3140019be709b94c71f1cc-prototype.
